title: Operator manages site keys from the web console
description:
The console has no site management whatsoever -- `console/app/` contains
`jobs`, `workers`, `login`, and `callback`, and nothing else. Minting a site
key, the single action every new publisher needs, is CLI-only. An operator
onboarding a site from a browser cannot do it.

The API already has `POST /sites`, `GET /sites`, and `DELETE /sites/{id}`.
This is a surface story, not a backend one.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Managing site keys from the web console

  Scenario: Operator lists site keys
    Given site keys exist for two origins
    When the operator opens the sites page
    Then each site is listed with its origin and site key

  Scenario: Operator mints a site key
    Given the operator is on the sites page
    When the operator creates a site for origin "https://example.com"
    Then the new site key is listed
    And the embed snippet for that site key is shown

  Scenario: Operator copies the embed snippet
    Given a site key exists
    When the operator copies its embed snippet
    Then the snippet contains that site key

  Scenario: Operator revokes a site key
    Given a site key exists
    When the operator revokes it and confirms
    Then it is no longer listed

  Scenario: Revoking a site key is guarded by confirmation
    Given a site key exists
    When the operator revokes it and cancels
    Then it is still listed
```

## Implementation brief

**`console/lib/api.ts`** — `fetchSites()`, `createSite(origin, name)`,
`revokeSite(identifier)`, plus a `Site` interface.

**`console/app/sites/page.tsx`** (new) — list, a create form (origin, optional
name), a per-row revoke with confirmation, and the embed snippet with a copy
control. Wrap in `AuthGuard` like the other pages.

**`console/components/Header.tsx`** — add the Sites nav entry.

**Embed snippet** — `cli/src/auritus/embed.py::format_embed_snippet` is the
canonical shape. Port it faithfully to TypeScript rather than improvising a
second snippet format; a divergence here ships broken copy-paste to
publishers. Consider whether the router should return the snippet so there is
one source of truth.

## Blocked on auritus-b0f217

That task establishes what a site's real identifier actually is. Today
`site create` prints `site_id=None` because the API response has no `id`
field, and `site revoke` works only because it passes whatever argument it
gets straight into `DELETE /sites/{arg}` and the site key happens to resolve.
The console must not be built on that ambiguity -- it needs to know which
value to put in the revoke call. Settle b0f217 first.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Implemented on feature/console-sites-page, merged to develop. New /sites page: create form, list with site_id/label/created_at/status, revoke with confirmation, and a one-time success callout showing the site_key plus the embed snippet (ported faithfully from cli/src/auritus/embed.py) with copy-to-clipboard -- correctly never re-displayed since GET /sites never returns site_key again. Header nav updated. Two things caught and fixed in review: (1) the agent's branch was created before feature/console-job-actions merged, and rebasing surfaced a real conflict in console/lib/api.ts where the stale diff would have deleted deleteJob/regenerateJob/retryJob -- resolved by keeping both; (2) the branch had accidentally committed Playwright's playwright-report/ and test-results/ output (only site/'s equivalents were gitignored, not console/'s) -- untracked them and extended .gitignore, which also protects the two prior console Playwright stories going forward. Also fixed a real style defect: the page used hardcoded Ant-Design-style hex colors (#52c41a, #cf1322, etc.) instead of this app's own --success/--danger/--ink-muted tokens that every other console page uses -- would have looked visually inconsistent. Independently re-verified: lint, tsc clean; ran the actual Playwright suite myself, 19/19 passing including all pre-existing job-detail tests (confirming the merge-conflict resolution didn't regress anything).
